it's THE site when you finish your job, at the end of the day. You can make beautifull cross-country in 'Belledonne' mountain, in the north.
It's often possible to hitch a ride from the LZ

spots.name: L'épine - lac d'aiguebelette
spots.takeoff_description:
alti:1150m
after 13h the breeze is coming. Thermic during the afternoon, great flight at the end of the day, over the Aiguebelette lake.
spots.going_there:
from Chambéry take the highway to Lyon. After the 'L'Épine' tunnel go out (Novalaise/Lac d'Aiguebelette, exit n°12). First crossroad on your left, and another time left immediately. Landing is just behind trees.
To go on the takeoff go to the 'col de l'Épine' pass with the D916 road. Just before the pass turn on your left and take a road on 3 km. Follow 'décollage' advertising.
spots.weather_notes:
The takeoff is under the wind if it's coming from the North, NE, E or SE.
Still flyable and possible to takeoff by North moderate wind (bellow 15km/h) but be careful by higher wind.
By any East component of wind you might find a gentle West breeze at takeoff to let you believe it is fine. Be extra careful, check the wind sock on tree top. You might be able to take off anyway but your flight might be rough and very uncomfortable (even dangerous).
spots.comments: good for child, there is a beautiful lake just near the site. No wind and hot water.

spots.name: Montlambert
spots.takeoff_description:
alti: 890m
after 12h thermals and breeze can be strong.
Lot's of pilots come here, we thank you to drive slowly and respect the people living on the road to the launch area. This site is fragile! If people complain too much we might lose the right to fly here.
So don't unload your car at the turning point on top. Do it when parked further down the road. Respect nature, the people and regulations!
spots.going_there:
Landing area: from Montmelian, take the N6 road. Turn to the left to 'Saint Jean de la Porte'. Before 'St Jean' turn to the left just after passing a bridge and go along a canal during 1 km. You have to cross a small bridge again.
Take off from landing area: at the end of the dirt road turn left. In 'Saint Jean de la Porte' turn left. After 1 or 2 km turn to the right, to Montlambert. In Montlambert turn back and and park your car, but not in the village! Walk 10 mn to the Southwest.
spots.weather_notes:
With North wind : The only site (with Courtet) where you can fly around Grenoble. But be careful with strong North wind (above ~20km/h) it's just a little protection and the wind can come quite suddenly. Also be careful when flying over ~1400m, the upper mountain protection can stop and you can find turbulences due to being on the lee side.
With SW wind or W wind, the take off is on the lee side of the takeoff's West side crest, if wind speed is low (below 10km/h) it might still be okay but not by stronger SW or W wind.
With W wind it's flyable, but it might be uncomfortable because of turbulences far above the valley.
In doubt, meet pilots on the site for advices.
spots.comments: This site is closed between mid September to beginning of November, because of an agreement with the local hunters. It is their best moment of joy, so again respect their fun as they do ours! Please inform yourselves about exact days of no-flying. On some days flying is still allowed.

spots.name: Saint Hilaire du Touvet
spots.takeoff_description:
North take off is a comfortable big carpet, but may be downwind of the thermic blowing in front.
South take off's in grass and you may find more facing thermal wind here than in north take off.
spots.going_there:
Take off is just near the funicular station in Saint Hilaire village. If you come from Grenoble, cross 'St Nazaire' and go to 'St Pancrasse'. Cross 'St Pancrasse' and turn to the right in St Hilaire village, after the fireman house. The takeoff is under a big chalet. The south takeoff : don't turn after fireman house but park your car on the parking, on your right after 100m. Walk on the track (5mn), take off is on your right.
Bus from/to Grenoble (sorry only in french) : http://chvd.org/spip.php?article63
It may be a wise idea to leave the car at the landing site and go up by the funicular. Timetables and prices: http://www.funiculaire.fr/
spots.weather_notes:
be careful with South wind.
In spring, conditions can be quite hard, specialy near the cliff.
spots.comments:
an easy XC:
after take off go to the south (your right). Follow the cliff and cross the 'Manival', a little valley. Work the first thermal and go up to the crest of 'Saint Eynard'. Follow this crest to the south until a beautifull old 'fort'. Come back with the same way. After 'Manival' valley you can go up the the 'Dent de Crolles' summit and follow the big crest to 'Le Granier' summit in the north direction. Come back at 'St hilaire' and land near your car :-))
spots.flight_rules:
You must not climb over 3000m.
This flight regulation is due to the Lyon International Airport proximity. Please don't mess with it !

spots.name: Agy plane
spots.takeoff_description: Strong Valley wind and thermic gusts. Nice grassy take off area, locals will be flying, read the FFVL site board-it's in French and English.
spots.going_there:
From Cluses->
follow the signs to  Les Gets/Morzine.
at Chatillon-sur-Cluses, turn right at the sign:
 Saint-Sigismond. At the end of Saint-Sigismond- turn left and follow the road all the way up to Agy Plane, get to the top of the mountain road and there is a little bar/restaurant - go further up and park by the Radio Tower/Satellite building.
spots.weather_notes:
1 >Bise wind-that strong NE wind that ruins most valley winds can have some effect.
2 >When Northerlies mix with valley wind if forecasted to blow hard, only good for small wings.
3 >Thermic gusts from the town of Cluses when entering the lower level valley wind and a somewhat technical landing if you approach in the peak of the valley wind, nice and smooth landing later in the evening.
spots.comments:
Endless XC routes.

Acro :
Known as Antoines secret training spot. Agy is the take off site above and to the side of the town Cluses. If training acro- the pilot has to make a short flight across from Agy to Chevran. Regardless of the met wind-the valley wind is sucked into Chamonix most good forecasted days when the sun shines, this valley wind displaces up Chevran Mountain in a mix of dynamic&thermic. Making it a mini magic mountain, Chevran is 600M high off the valley floor and in general a pilot on an acro wing would have anything from 600m to 800m vertical once pushing out from Chevran above Cluses. Beware of the diagonal drift towards the mountain in a maneuver. In a rescue situation the trees of Chevran would be the landing point but with a Rogallo, there is space to land below the foot of the Mountain.
spots.flight_rules: delicate LZ! absolutely avoid out-landing!!

spots.name: Barneville sur seine
spots.takeoff_description:
There are two starting directions: 
30° has a nice, long, shallow and well maintained meadow but (!) this meadow is surrounded by high trees. the only obvious way out is a tiny gap at the bottom at ~35°.
330° has no slope at all. a flat top of great meadow grass abruptly turns into a cliff full of nettles. Due to the form of the neighboring slopes all NW winds are channeled up that cliff.
spots.going_there:
GPS finds the starting position quite well. the rest is easy.
No official access to the current landing.  'atterisage delta' only accessible 
via Yville sur Seine.

spots.name: Bisanne Sud
spots.takeoff_description:
alti: 1940m 
It is near the altitude restaurant. This takeoff is on the top, on the South-East side. Just next to the parking.
spots.going_there:
from 'Albertville', go to 'Les Saisies'. You can stop at the landing area. After go to 'Les Saisies' 
By car : turn to the left when you arrive in this ski station. Keep the road to the end, there is an Altitude restaurant on the top.
During winter or sping when there is still a lot of snow (up to around beginning of May), the road to the takeoff is unusable by car, but you can use the chairlift, there are one way tickets for paragliders.
During summer (July and August) there are (in 2020 : free) buses that you can use from to go from the Valley (Beaufort or Villard sur Doron) to Les Saisies. Then you can use the chairlift (open in July and August) to reach the takeoff

More info somewhere on there site :
https://www.lessaisies.com

In 2020 the information page is here (but it changes every now and then) :
https://www.lessaisies.com/bus-albertville-navettes-intramuros-gratuites.html
spots.weather_notes: Later in the day the breeze might be stronger than the thermals and be coming in your back.
spots.comments:
It might happen that your arrive too late at this takeoff (like 12am or later) and the valley breeze is already blowing from the back (North)
Then there is an alternate takeoff (check the map), that can also be used with North wind from which you can still takeoff and reach the south face (in the lee side).
Discouraged with strong North wind !

A good idee to go to 'Aravis', in spring. Beaufortain is a good district for family holidays: a lots of differents activities.
You can finish your day in 'Le Cormet de Roselend', a soaring site. You will fly until the night with the breeze!

spots.name: Clamontard - Luc-en-Diois
spots.takeoff_description:
North -also good with NW and NE.
Often there is a West component, so the TO is in the lee: watch the different windspies very closely, turn immediately left after launching.

To get there: 7 KM to TO:
From Luc-en-Diois follow direction Gap (south);
after the big rocks and the Drome river bridge, turn right (signs: 'site d'envol').
After 2 Km you will see a sign and an unpaved road on your left, follow it till the end.
spots.weather_notes:
West wind make launch (take off) hazardous

Wind info (also on FFVL frequency):
- http://balisemeteo.com/depart.php?dept=26
- http://balisemeteo.com/balise.php?idBalise=33

spots.name: Déco Baisse de Raymond (Veillos)
spots.takeoff_description:
There are several take-offs at La Colmiane, but the most often used are the two described below: 

Veillos 
There are actually two south-facing 'Veillos' launches, that are located on spines of the Mont Pétoumier - Mont Pépoiri ridge north of La Colmiane. All summer there is a Navette from the Veillos chairlift, and the chairlift itself is in use.You can also drive up: 

From La Colmiane, head out on the D2565 towards St Dalmas. On the very first sharp left-hand U-bend in the road, there is a minor road that goes straight. Take this. It immediately splits into two forks, the right-hand one of which is the track up to take-off. (There is a chain across the bottom - replace this after you). You pass 2 hang-glider launches as you zig-zag up the hillside, and the road eventually flattens out and goes into the back of the bowl. Continue here, going left on the main track when the road goes right to a refuge. The road follows the ridge-line to its end, and then zig-zags up again. You can park at the top of the zig-zags. Take-off is the grassy area above the road. 

Le Pic de Colmiane 
From the col at la Colmiane, drive up the dirt track that goes to Col du Suc, which is signed 'Parapente'. Drive past the first streamered area - the better takeoff is higher up. You can park in the obvious area where the road goes over the col, and walk up the footpath which goes to the top of the chairlift. Launch is just below the chairlift, and is a clear, grassy area marked by windsocks.
spots.going_there: D2205. 5 km before St Saveur de Tinée, turn off on the D2565 on the right, which goes to La Colmiane. You reach the small village of St Dalmas about 2km before arriving at La Colmiane ski station. The football field in St Dalmas, known as 'Le Soun Pra', is the official landing field, and is signposted from the village. Libuelle, the paragliding school, have a bulletin board on their building in the landing field. This shows the locations of the main take-offs and landings.
spots.weather_notes: Beware that wind can easily switch from coming up to coming over the back of the col above the main landing therefore you should check the wind direction on approach. The valley is also pretty well protected but the surrounding valeys are narrow, this should be taken into account if leaving the area and flying XC
spots.comments:
La Colmiane lies south of the boundary to the Mercantour National Park, approximately 40km almost directly north of Nice. It is within easy reach of the large mountains to the North and the views once high are spectacular, reaching into Italy.

spots.name: Escalette
spots.takeoff_description:
A very short take off on a rocky & dry ground. You need to take off facing the wing. 

This position won't take you directly to the landing spot, so you have to make sure the local dynamic wind will give you enough altitude. Ask the locals how to do it.
spots.going_there: Park your car at the 'Parking de l'En Chois', follow the red marked trail. It will take you to the 'Pas de L'escalette'. 200m before getting there, you will see white fences boarding the trail. Make a left just before. It will take you off trail for 150m and get you to the take off. Don't expect to find it by yourself the first time, but you will likely see wings there.
spots.weather_notes: Perfect site for soaring by the end of the day. Needs S and SW wind, avoid any other condition.
spots.comments:
People usually meet at the parking at around 5:30pm during summer.

A very technical site.

spots.name: Garlaban
spots.takeoff_description: The take-offs are quite short but do not present any particular difficulties.
spots.going_there: On the A501 motorway linking Marseille to Aix en Provence via Aubagne, exit at exit 7, join the big roundabout and take the D96 for about a hundred metres. Then take the Chemin des Solans to a small roundabout where you have to turn left to stay on the Chemin des Solans. At the end of this road, at the end of the paved road, you will find a dirt DFCI track on the right that leads to a dirt parking with two large green tanks. This is where you should stop and consult the Site information panel. (Geographical coordinates of the car park: N43°19'27.67" / E 5°33'31.93"). Access to the decos is by foot, it takes about 40 minutes to walk. Access to the landing by vehicle is strictly prohibited.
spots.weather_notes:
General orientation: East to South. Dangerous in North, NW and NE winds and in Westerly winds. Favourable with easterly, east-south-easterly, south-south-easterly and south-south winds. 

In breezy conditions and in the absence of strong weather winds, flight is possible in the middle of the morning. However, the southwest sea breeze returns fairly quickly at midday, more or less early depending on the season due to the proximity of the sea, making flying turbulent and inadvisable.
spots.comments: Presence of a quiet area for the protection of the Bonelli's eagle. This area does not apply to the site for local flight. It is located 5km from the takeoff, in the municipality of Gémenos, heading east. This type of "upwind" flight is unlikely and of no interest.
spots.flight_rules:
A prefectoral decree regulates access to the Bouches du Rhône mountains during the summer period from 1 June to 30 September. In the orange period access is free, in the red period it is limited between 6am and 11am, and in the black period any penetration is strictly prohibited and punishable by a contravention. Information on 0811 20 13 13 13 or on the website http://www.bouches-du-rhone.pref.gouv.fr/index.php 

Flights possible during the hunting season except on days when game is released (see calendar on the information panel on the website). 

The site is located in the TMA Marseille Provence 6 (ceiling limited to 1370 m altitude (4500 feet).

spots.takeoff_description:
The main (lower) take-off is a 30 min walk from Gréolières village. The school runs a navette service (from 9 am) to this or to the upper TO in summer. Ski station chair lifts from the resort of Gréolières-les-Neiges can be used to access this upper take-off in winter. 

300, main launch
30 minute walk from the schoollanding field, or use the Navette service from here. 

600 and 700
1 hour's walk from Greolieres-les-Neiges or Navette from the school landing field. 4x4 access in private vehicles is not allowed. 

1000 Cheiron summit 
1h20 walk from the school landing field. Chairlifts from the ski station at Greolieres-les-Neiges can be used in winter. 

Navette Prices
Le Dahut (lower takeoff) 5 Euros or ½ ticket 
700 or Jerusalem (upper) 8 Euros or 1 ticket. 
10 tickets = 60 Euros
spots.weather_notes: Valley winds at the landing field are usually from the east. If there is a westerly blowing, the site gets very turbulent and it is not advisable to fly.
spots.comments:
With a high-point of 1770m, the Cheiron is the biggest and most obvious ridge in this area (Look out for it as you fly over on the approach to Nice airport!). It is a very reliable site, with year-round thermals pulling the air up the front even when the clouds are scooting over the top from the north (but be prepared to encounter this wind if you fly above cliff height). It offers both dynamic lift and thermals all year round. 

In terms of XC, it is not the easiest site to get away from, but there is a straight-forward 15km out-and-return ridge-run to Coursegoules that is very achievable on a reasonable day. The accessibility of the site, and that it is so often flyable, coupled with the magnificent views of Mediterranean, the snow-capped Mercantour and the ski-slopes on the north side of the mountain are reason enough to fly here for most!.

Informations from http://www.flyozone.com/paragliders/de/infozone/fly-gourdon/greolieres/

spots.takeoff_description:
Décollage pour le parapente et un pour le deltaplane. Vent : S et SE/SO

S'attendre a un thermique en sortie de déco. Et donc faire une tempo / coup de frein.  Tenir sa voile.
spots.going_there:
Montpellier : direction Ganges. Turn in Cazilhac-Le-Haut then take a dirt road for 40 minutes. 

There is a shuttle going to the take-off site once per day on most days that are flyable. The shuttle usually leaves around 13h from Coupiac (the landing spot). The shuttle is operated by the club 'Les ailes de la Seranne'. To see if the shuttle is running on a particular day, post to the discussion thread here or contact the club.

It is also possible to walk up to the takeoff site, either by the road or using one of several footpaths. You should count 1 or 1.5 hours, depending on your condition.

http://les-ailes-de-la-seranne.fr/
spots.weather_notes: You can fly with N and NW wind but it can be strong suddenly so be careful. Tune your radio to the frequency 143.98.75 to hear the updated wind information broadcast every 10 minutes
spots.comments:

Good XC site

spots.name: le Chalvet (Saint Andre les Alpes)
spots.takeoff_description: The main launch SW/ W is relatively steep, and thermic from around midday. The wind on take-off can be strong, particularly later on when the valley winds become established. When the thermic activity dies down again, very pleasant evening soaring is often available until it gets dark. South-East launches are easy, very large.
spots.going_there:
There is a good (but narrow) paved road (The C30) up to Le Chalvet take-off from the NW side of the town, but this is often snowed in from December to March. For parking, there is a lay-by close to the S take-off, and places for several cars at the end of the road beneath the South-West launch. The Lakeside landing area / Aerogliss HQ is reached by taking the road to Nice out of St Andre, and turning left by the supermarket. This link takes you to a local map up to take off and intro about the site: http://flystandre.com/flying-services/chalvet-site-intro/
Normally shuttle buses operate from the LZ.
spots.weather_notes: Lake landing can be turbulent in a rather strong N or NW meteo wind (Mistral). In fact, by light Mistral, no troubles by starting from the SW launch, but when conditions are getting only windy,we oftenly catch a microwave. with a light North, it is flyable too (North launch), but no real interest. Wind info (alos on FFVL frequency): http://www.balisemeteo.com/depart.php?dept=04 http://www.balisemeteo.com/balise.php?idBalise=109 For full access to all the Saint Andre weather including wind speed on launch etc on a single page visit: http://flystandre.com/webcam-weather/
spots.comments: St Andre is a well-known flying site, having been used for international paragliding and hang gliding events for years. It is renowned for its strong thermals and good cross country potential, with routes to the north to Dormillouse, Briancon, Allos etc, and south to Col de Bleyne. The main (SW) launch tends to blow out for paragliders when conditions get really thermic and the valley breezes get strong, so cross country-seekers need to aim to be on launch for 11:30 to 13:00, ready for the sun to begin pulling thermals up the SW face. For those seeking gentler conditions, there are E and SE-facing launches for morning flights, and evening flying until sunset from the SW launch can be very rewarding. There is a good road to top, but it is often snowed in during the winter (Dec to Mar). Note: St Andre is not an FFVL flying site. Aerogliss administer the site, and ask that all visiting pilots contact them before flying. (Their base is in next to the lakeside landing field. Contact details given below).
spots.flight_rules: Groups and schools have to contact Aerogliss before coming. +33 492891130 or divers@aerogliss.com

strong  thermals in summer

spots.takeoff_description: nice and easy take off, grass, nice slope, what you ll have to worry of is more likely to be the aerological conditions
spots.going_there:
coming from perpignan, continue heading 'andora'. You ll cross 'targasonne' village. at the exit of targasonne, the shop 'ailipse' is on your left  100m before the circle, ask them for some info.
If they re not here, take right at the circle, follow the road like 500m and you ll see the landing on your right.
You can walk straight up to the take off, or take off at mid-height.
There is a track to the top but its access is reglemented, you must go at 'Ailipse' in order to drive up.
spots.weather_notes:
The site may sometimes be at the meeting point of breezes from tree valleys : cerdagne (south west), Tet (East), and Capcir (North) : if wind conditions change at take off, it may fast become a bit weird on the site so be carefull.
thermics may start near the landing area : keep your attention all the landing progress long untill you re on the ground.
spots.comments:
Very nice thermic site, can be the start for XC in the cerdagne valley if you have enough height.
The Cerdagne valley breeze is south west oriented and may blow strong in hot afternoons.

spots.name: Montaud
spots.takeoff_description:
On the road from Montaud to Autrans, before Mortier tunel (road really closed : take off not accessible from Autrans).
Montaud village is 5 km south from Voreppe -via Veurey- 15 km NW from Grenoble.
Take off is on road side ... no walking !
Impressive for beginners : good slope, not too wide, but no real danger if breeze is present.
spots.going_there:
from 'Voreppe' direction 'Lans en Vercors'. In 'Veurey', after cross Isere river, take the 'Montaud' direction. drive 5km.
Once arrived on the plateau, cross the first residential area then turn right to the sports facilities and park here.
spots.weather_notes:
While take off is NW oriented, fly there by N or even NE. Take care at NW and avoid W :
dangers come from wind along the cliffs, W oriented.
spots.comments:
Caution, altitude is limited, due to airways :
- 1900 m over Bec d'Orient (W of take off),
- 2800 m over take off,
the limit is between both.
spots.flight_rules: Please be really respectful while driving across the inhabited places !

spots.takeoff_description:
huge, easy

Other TO 'Courchon' at N43.84278, E6.23028, 905m available: rather flat, stony: not so easy in low winds
spots.going_there:
Take the D952 out of Moustiers towards Riez. The road climbs up a series of bends, after which there is a turning on the right-hand side that is signed 

Navette from LZ (Venasque) normally at 1045, 1645) (price: 6EUR/ pers in 2013)

It is possible to drive almost to TO, park when you arrive at the 'fence', afterwards it's hardcore 4x4
spots.weather_notes:
Breeze coming from the lake (west) and could be strong in summer.
In summer between 1300-1700 it can get very strong/ bumpy - beware of eventual dust devils at LZ.
Wind info for Moustiers (also on FFVL frequency):
http://www.balisemeteo.com/depart.php?dept=04
http://www.balisemeteo.com/balise.php?idBalise=130
spots.comments:
Very sweet site: you can stay on the crest in local thermal or go on the front, on flat land XC. If you want adventure, go in your back, Saint André direction ;-) but coming back by road is a little bit difficult!
And your family can have good time on the Sainte Croix lake (beach) or in Verdon valley (climbing, rafting, walking...)

spots.name: Plaine Joux (Passy)
spots.takeoff_description:
At Plaine Joux.
Wide take off, nicely prepared.
Can be windy the afternoon (valley brise)
spots.going_there:
Getting to launch site:
1) by car, approx 15min drive up. If you are alone, try to ask around, possibly there may be other pilot(s) willing to go up, so one car you can keep at landing. 
2) by shuttle. On the weekend days you can find some vans offering shuttle service, or if you are kind you can join the vans of tandem flights or school.
2020: Public bus (SAT) L85  is available to go to the take off: the bus stop is on Chedde market place. 3,5 € until Guébriant and 6 € until Plaine-Joux (about 950m walk after Guébriant stop) link to the L85 timetable: http://www.sat-montblanc.com/horaire-timetables/ligne-85-sallanches-plateau-d-assy-pleine-joux.aspx


3) Walking. It is approximately 1,5hr walk from the landing site of Chedde. Walk up to the road which goes to Servoz, then walk towards Servoz (1km) until find footpath with indicator to Plaine Joux. Then walk up.
spots.weather_notes:
Avoid flying with strong west, south west wind. 
With west wind coming, the landing is hard to reach, and conditions can be really turbulent.


Very well protected from north wind. It is still flyable even with insane north wind.

Usually west wind is related to foehn. 
ALWAYS check Foehn before flying: VERY turbulent conditions if Foehn is NOT between -4 hPa and +4 hPa. Check foehn forecast on http://www.meteocentrale.ch/fr/meteo/foehn-et-bise/foehn.html
spots.comments: Chedde landing site is usually more crowded, higher chances of getting shuttles from there.
spots.flight_rules:
The cliff behind the takeoff is part of the national park - it is not allowed to fly closer than 300m from it. The cliff more to the to the west is OK to fly close.

At both landing sites the approach should be the standard 'C' approach, please respect this rule as the sky over the landing fields, especially Chedde, is often very crowded.

At landing sites the kiting should be interrupted when pilots are on the approach.

At the Marlioz landing site the hang gliders have got the prioriity on the approach.

ATTN: if flying towards Chamonix/ Mont Blanc: observe flight restrictions: no TO, landing and overflight! (>> see pix)
> France
- LF R30B: July-August
- LF R30A: permanent
> Italy: 4.8. - 15.9.2016

spots.takeoff_description: Yes
spots.going_there: Depuis Besançon centre ville (Chamars), prendre la direction de Lyon. Environ 100 m avant le panneau de fin d'agglomération de Besançon, prendre le pont qui mène à Velotte. Prendre la rue à gauche à environ 100 m de la sortie du pont et suivre la rive droite du Doubs. Passer sous le pont de la N 273 et prendre tout de suite à droite. Suivre la direction du Fort de Planoise. Arrivé au fort, suivre la flèche « Emmaüs », vers la droite. Le décollage est juste en face.
spots.comments: Le site est très sain et facile, tant en parapente qu'en delta, par vent de Nord-Est qui est l'un des vents dominants dans la région. Cependant par vent de nord il faut se méfier des éventuels rouleaux dus à la côte située à gauche du décollage. De même par vent d'est des rouleaux peuvent apparaître, dus aux reliefs situés à l'est (Montfaucon notamment). Dans ces deux cas il faut rejoindre l'atterrissage des Craies en « sautant » la côte située à droite du décollage avant d'avoir perdu trop d'altitude ; l'atterrissage est juste derrière. Un atterrissage de dépannage peut être utilisé : le terrain de Base-Ball situé à gauche du décollage. En cas de gros problème il est possible de se poser dans une friche située à droite du terrain de Base Ball. Éviter les serres situées sous le décollage !

spots.name: Reinhardsmunster
spots.takeoff_description:
460 meters.
When arriving in Reinhardsmunster turn left onto the road to Obersteigen. 1 km later, GO STRAIGHT AHEAD and follow the forest road which leads to a car park at an intersection (6 km). 
Once parked turn south and you can choose one of 2 paths that lead to the takeoff. The main one is the one behind the wooden ramp/gate: walk 100m along a forest road then there's a small path going right and diagonally up  the hill for another 100m to the takeoff. There's an INFO PANEL just as you arrive, READ IT :) 
An alternative path from the parking is parallel and above the first one. It starts 20m to the west of the ramp. Always stay left and when you exit the forest and walk another 50m you'll see the takeoff on your left. 

Large and relatively easy take off. A bit steep, covered with astroturf(carpet). Slippery when wet! 

Landing on the right not visble until you take off.

For HG landing is better on the left, at the practice area/spot. Can be seen from the takeooff.
spots.weather_notes:
Take off a very technical, can be dangerous, in strong wind. 

Magic lift fenomenon on some days in the evening.
spots.comments:
XC to Haut Barr castle (up north) is a classic.

Max. height : 1520m

Flights are NOT ALLOWED from monday 06h00 friday 15h00 (military zone).

Access to the site is strictly FORBIDDEN in September (deers fornication ...).
spots.flight_rules:
Airspace during the weekdays: YOU MUST contact the Phalsbourg airbase (Tél. 03 87 25 21 53) !!! if you are the fist OR last to fly/land!!!
see airspace image in the PHOTOS.
Do not take off after 30 minutes prior to sunset. In september (ususally the whole month) the site is CLOSED due to the "Brame du Cerf"  the annual deer breeding time. Check with the local pilots and/or contact numbers on the Flying site information pannel (on the takeoff and landing).

This site is not for beginners!! Take off is short and in a strong slope, top landing may be tricky !!

spots.name: Sospel - Agaisen
spots.takeoff_description: The Agaisen launch, which faces SW, is perfect for going XC from. The locals call it \'The Lift\', for its large, regular thermals, and people have flown to Saint-Andre from here (appx 75km).
spots.going_there:
Sospel is most easily reached from the Menton exit of the A8 along the D2566, but you could also take the RD2204 from Nice.


Mt Agaisen: Once in Sospel, take the road signposted to the college. A left turning from this road climbs to Mont Agaisen. The road is tarmaced or concreted all the way to the top, and is suitable for all vehicles.
spots.comments:
Sospel is 40km (30 minutes) NE of Nice, or 15 minutes from Menton. It lies in the heart of the Bevera valley, protected by a cirque of mountains which surround it. It is very close to both the borders of the Mercantour National park, and of Italy. You are not allowed to fly in the National park itself (unless you are more than 1000m above the ground!), and this rule is taken very seriously by park wardens. 

The views from on high are amazing: Mont Mangiabo to the north, Italy to the east and the Mediterranean Sea to the south. On a clear day you can see the point of Saint Tropez to the west.

spots.takeoff_description:
Several takeoff points to suit wind direction.
Launch from either side of gorge with good lift from sheer faces.
Easy access to takeoff points. No need to carry your gear too far!!
Gorge is about 300 metres above valley floor.

Plusieurs décollages en fonction de la direction du vent, des deux côtés des gorges. Bonne composante verticale (parois abruptes).
 Accès facile aux points de décollage. Pas besoin de transporter votre équipement trop loin!
 Décollage environ 300 mètres au-dessus du fond de la vallée.
spots.going_there:
Drive south (1.5 days from Home Counties) or fly to either Toulouse or Rodez. (Rodez is Ryanair from London Stanstead and Toulouse is Easyjet, BA etc from London Gatwick.Low cost carriers also fly from Bristol and Southampton. There are flights from other airports further north but seem to be seasonal.)
St Antonin is 1hr 15min drive from Toulouse and Rodez.
spots.weather_notes:
Non that I can see but I'm no expert. It seems to suit beginners and experts alike.
Check the website..For Hang Gliding and in French but looks like good info regarding takeoff and windsock location etc.
spots.comments:
I live opposite the 2 main flying sites and it looks as if you can stay up as long as you like!

The photograph shows 12 paragliders and 2 hang-gliders up at the same time... this is very rare! Must have been a good day! Sometimes busy at weekends but during the week.... sky's the limit!

spots.name: Ste Anastasie
spots.takeoff_description:
Large take off place on the St Quinis massif.
South side, visible from Landing place.

Possibility to land near the take off.
Needs good skill of landing on small area.
High trees all around.

Details here: 
https://tasie-parapente.club/le-site/

ONLY 4x4 vehicles can use the very bad track leading to take off.
spots.going_there:
Landing place is located on North side of Sainte Anastasie sur Issole village.
Between railroad and St Quinis massif.
Car-park available on the landing place.

Take off access walking on a stony path climbing to the relief (about 20Mn, 1000m distance, 180m level).
spots.weather_notes:
Flyable site when wind is coming from SSE & S.
For E & O winds impossible to fly due to high downwind on the relief.
spots.flight_rules:
WARNING !!!
Site on a military zone where helicopters are flying a lot.

Flyable only if authorization is allowed by the military base.
Info given everyday on the club website must be read before to go to the take off: https://tasie-parapente.club/le-site/

Normally, if our area is open, we must fly on the space allowed and limited to level 650m ASL above sea level) about 15m above highest relief summit of St Quinis. 

Radio equipment is mandatory to fly here, tuned on FFVL frequency (143.9875 Mhz).

Thanks to respect those rules for maintaining the site flyable.

Local pilots will be happy to inform you.

spots.takeoff_description: Drive to the ski sation, outside the times that the ski lift doesn't run. Otherwise, take the lift, take off is immediately on the left on the slope next to the derelict church. Steep, but easy. Wind will be light so forward is needed sometimes.

spots.weather_notes:
Southwind is dangerous. Lots of turbulence. Strong valley wind in the afternoon. 
Fly Lac d'Oo instead and come back evening for a nice valley wind soar.
spots.comments:
Absolutely Amazing flying. Ask a Pro for advice.
Close to an airfield, regulated flying for landing approach. Please read the posted guidelines on the notice board.

If you are experienced enough, in the afternoon, when the breeze eases off a little, you can cross to the other side of the valley, soaring 'the road' all the way up and then plenty of possibilities to make it far enough into the valley against the wind.
Take care, serious turbulence is possible.

spots.name: Thorenc - Col de Bleyne
spots.takeoff_description:
alti:1525m
Approximately 400m top to bottom. 

Beware of snagging lines on stones / shrubs on take-off. The wind can switch direction slightly, making launching a little tricky if you catch it at the wrong moment.
spots.going_there:
From Nice, head east along the A8 and take the Cagnes sur Mer exit. Then either follow the D6 from la Colle sur Loup to GrÃƒÂ©oliÃƒÂ¨res through the Gorges du Loup, or come through Vence and via Coursegoules on the D236 and then the D2. From GrÃƒÂ©oliÃƒÂ¨res, take the road to Thorenc and climb up to the Col de Bleyne. At the Col, a track breaks off right and goes all the way to take-off. 

The take-off you see is CDB1 (for these purposes - not an official name). To get to CDB2 there is a short walk on a path through the trees to the east.
spots.weather_notes: It can be turbulent in a westerly - better to decamp to Lachens.
spots.comments:
The site record is held by David Dagault for a 257km flight to Megeve on 8th May 1998. 
Col de Bleyne is a southerly-facing site with a 400m top-to-bottom and excellent XC potential. There are an abundance of big fields to land in both in its own valley, and along the route to Saint AndrÃƒÂ©, although in spring and early summer grass is grown as crop, and fields containing it should be avoided. The Montagne de Thorenc is best flown in a light southerly meteo wind direction, although on a good, light-wind day thermals will be drawn up the front regardless. 

The site is primarily a thermic site, so is most often used in Spring and summer, although people have been known to thermal there above snow-covered fields in winter!

Informations from http://www.flyozone.com/site_guide/cdb.asp
spots.flight_rules: Be careful, take off is very near the Nice TMA.

spots.name: Cagnorina - Tende- Tenda
spots.takeoff_description:
From Tende, take the road for La Pia, and follow the 'Parapente' signs to take-off. (This is about a 15 minute drive). You will pass a stadium on the way up, which can be used as a landing area in early mornings or evenings, but becomes too turbulent for use during the day. 

Col de Tende: Turn immediately left after the Tende tunnel on the N204. Cross the '3 Amis' station, and climb up to the col on a good road (30 minutes from Tende).
spots.going_there: From Nice, take the A8 east to Ventimiglia, and join the N204 through the Gorges de Saorge to Tende.
spots.comments:
Tende is at the end of the Roya valley, about 50km north of Nice. It lies very close to the boundaries of the Mercantour national Park, which must not be overflown by paraglider (except at >1000m AGL). 

There are two main sites: Cagnorina is just above the town itself, and Col de Tende is a few kilometres north of Tende, right on the Italian border. The col can be flown on either the south or the north sides.

spots.name: Gourdon
spots.takeoff_description: L'embarnier - a SE-facing rugged ridge, actually two takeoffs, a small one right next to the parking with a big rock in its midst, another one, large and easy, reachable by a short walk up the ridge.
spots.weather_notes:
Although SE-facing, this site is protected by the sea breeze and is generally flyable even with a moderate NW,N or NE meteo wind above. 

The site can be turbulent in a strong northerly meteo wind. Southerly wind reinforces the sea breeze.

In spring/summer, conditions usually get quite strong at midday, but that is lunch time anyway.
spots.comments:
Gourdon is 20km from the sea as the crow flies (and about 37km by road). The ridge reaches 1250m at its highest point, and has two take-offs, the upper of which is slightly bigger, both facing south-east. Because of the sea breeze, there is often dynamic lift to augment the thermic lift, and cross-countries are possible all year round. Convergence often sets up right over the site. The SE orientation means that you can launch early, and local pilots often leave Gourdon and reach Col de Bleyne just as that site is beginning to work. 

You can drive all the way to take-off (carefully!) on a rough track, and top land, making it a very convenient site. It is also very popular, which makes it relatively easy to hitch back up to the top, but also means it can be very crowded at weekends.
spots.flight_rules:
This site is below the Nice Airport airspace, limiting it to FL65, so stay below 2000m. 

More prohibited airspace (Nice and Cannes CTRs) towards the sea, to the south of the Valettes landing.

spots.takeoff_description:
Leave the A8 at La Turbie, and follow the signs for the Monte Carlo golf club. Turn right at the Monte-Carlo radio antennae. Parking is limited (10 places) and hitching back up for a vehicle difficult. It makes sense to use the navette (euro1), which leaves from the car park opposite the train station (close to the landing area) between 10am and 4pm (10am, 11.15, 14.00 15.15 - only Oct-April). BEWARE OF FLYING RESTRICTIONS ( NOTAM, ZIT MENTON) ALWAYS CHECK Roquebrunailes website or fb BEFORE TAKING OFF. 

If you see white waves on the see, just don't take off or if you are already flying, go to the landing quick.
spots.going_there:
Hike from beach takes 1 hour 20-30min

2020/02 
Official paragliding shuttle : Line G (4€ a lift, 10€ the day). 
NOT AVAILABLE ON TUESDAYS&WEDNESDAYS. 
You have to "ACTIVATE IT" (phone or at the bus office) at least 2h before or the day before 18h for the first lift in the morning.

From 1st october to 15th november and in april: 10H - 11H45 - 14H30 - 16H00.
From 16th november to 31th of march: 09H30 - 11H15 - 14H00 - 15H30.

The way back is included in the ticket. 

link to the official pdf  https://www.zestbus.fr/fileadmin/mediatheque/Keolis/__SITES_TEMPORAIRES__/keolis_menton/Documents/Fiches_Horaires/LIGNE_G__20SEPT.pdf
spots.weather_notes:
The beach landing can be turbulent in an easterly wind. Do not launch if there are 'white horses' on the sea - it is too windy!
Detailed wx info here: http://www.roquebrunailes.com/en/local-aerology-roquebrune.htm
Wx forcast here: http://www.roquebrunailes.com/en/weather-forecast-roquebrune.htm

LIVE WIND SENSOR: http://www.balisemeteo.com/balise.php?idBalise=163
spots.comments:
This is a very spectacular place to fly, as you launch from a carpeted take-off and fly down over the rooftops and swimming pools of Monaco, to land on the beach, perhaps being watched from the beach-side cafe by one of the many rich & famous whose home this is.
informations from http://www.flyozone.com/site_guide/roquebrune.asp
spots.flight_rules:
local by-law, 2020.
take off open to:
- people older than 16 years,
- school's students with 2 official instructors (one at take off, one at landing)
- pilote with at least parapro4/ippi4
- glide with a wing loading below 5kg/m² (mini wing forbidden, if you are a test pilote you can ask the club for derogation)

site open:
November 15 to April 30 : without restrictions.
May 1st to June 30 : before 8h and after 18h (possible changes to better autorisation, check updates on Roquebrunaile website regularly) 
July 1st to August 31 : before 8h and after 19h.
September 1st to Sept 30 : before 8h and after 18h.
October 1st to November 15 : after 11h15.

Pilots on the take-off area must to be ready to fly. Use the surface of preparation to connect your glide with harness, or other.

Flight above take-off forbidden.

Top-landing only on the main take-off.

Professionals instructors must:
- be in rule with 'jeunesse et sport' ministry,
- have a professional insurance,
- have a authorization from the town hall.

fly above houses: more than 100m;

fly above military base forbidden;

Acro and SIV maneuvers forbidden;
more informations (french local club):
http://www.roquebrunailes.com/en/regulation-roquebrune.htm

Max Altitude: 1981m/amsl or max 305 above ground!!!! See map here: http://www.roquebrunailes.com/en/free-flighing-alpes-maritimes.htm

spots.name: Auron
spots.takeoff_description:
alti: 2274m
The summit of Cime de la Bercha can be gained via a cable car from St Etienne de Tinée, or by a rough track from Auron. 

Las Donnas is reachable by a cable car from Auron. It is on the south side of Auron, so in the mornings when you can launch facing N or E you can land in the Auron valley, but once it becomes thermic you\'ll be on the south side of the mountain. It is easy to land in the small village of Roya, which is served by a road (the D61), but advisable to arrange a retrieve before doing so! 

The cable cars work all winter, and also in July and August.
spots.going_there: Auron can be reached from Nice by taking St Isidore exit of the A8 onto the N202. Follow this north (towards Digne) until it joins the D2205 at the entrance to the Gorges de la Mescla. From here, take the D2205, signed Isola and Auron, all the way to Auron and St Etienne de Tinée.
spots.comments:
Auron is a mountain village about 90km NNW of Nice, which is very popular as a winter ski resort. It sits in a little pocket that is not included in the Parc National du Mercantour. It is just south of the town of St Etienne de Tinée, on the D2205. La Cime de la Berchia (2270m) is the principal launch site of Auron, providing a good high-altitude launch point which can be reached by cable car in winter, or by track, with great cross country potential. 

Note that paragliding and other aerial sports are banned in the National park itself (unless you are at an altitude of greater than 1000m above the ground) so be aware of its borders. 

Weather information is posted in the cable car station and the St Etienne de Tinée tourist office. 

informations from http://www.flyozone.com/site_guide/auron.asp

You have to glide over the trees and just after the power kick your wing. In the morning go to right, near the golf, in afternoon and after go at left close to the cliff.

spots.going_there:
Montpellier : direction Ganges. Turn in Cazilhac-Le-Haut then take a dirt road for 40 minutes. 

There is a shuttle going to the take-off site once per day on most days that are flyable. The shuttle usually leaves around 13h from Coupiac (the landing spot). The shuttle is operated by the club 'Les ailes de la Seranne'. To see if the shuttle is running on a particular day, post to the discussion thread here or contact the club.

It is also possible to walk up to the takeoff site, either by the road or using one of several footpaths. You should count 1 or 1.5 hours, depending on your condition.

http://les-ailes-de-la-seranne.fr/

spots.weather_notes:
Usable in almost any flyable conditions but its full potential is unleashed the morning (S-E face).
As the day progressed, the valley breeze becomes stronger and stronger, making it harder and uncomfortable to find thermals.

In conditions of strong North wind (NW,N,NE), reaching the upper crest might prove quite uncomfortable (Lee side). You can still escape however lower than the crest, but that's trickier

Only 2 or 3 wings can simultaneously take off but the field is wide enough for every one to prepare their wings.
Due to the valley breeze, the wind at takeoff is almost allways coming front.
Tall trees at end of take off, not exactly beginners friendly...

spots.name: Leucate -Sémaphore Falaise EST
spots.takeoff_description:
Inside a little valley and just front of the 'Sémaphore' you can find the take off (NE-E orientation). It's also possible to take off on the second face of the valley, 5o meters further, with an orientation SE. But be careful : maximum orientation with SE is 125°. Don't fly over that orientation.
Generally :
Minimum wind fly is 17 km/h.
Higher fly are between 25 and 30 km/h 
Maximum wind fly is 35 km/h.
Timing : 12h to 15h.
spots.going_there: Between 'leucate village' and 'leucate plage' turn the way in direction of the lighthouse. On the top, park your car and walk less than 10 mn long of the cliff to the 'Sémaphore'
spots.weather_notes: The wind can stop quickly sometimes. You fly 40m up to the top in general. If it's your first time, go landing when you're around 25m high.
spots.comments: Observe the white-capped waves. They're very important to see the wind force and easy to understand. If they're just front of the beach it's to late. Land before they arrive front of the beach.
spots.flight_rules: Fly NE to ESE. Perfect laminar wind with zero surprise. Don't fly under 17 km/h. If you fall down, for your security, it's possible to land on the beach, but it's prohibited. Because it's really small, it's very dangerous for vacationers and you. So, Please respect every body!

spots.name: Montgirod-Arcachat
spots.takeoff_description:
2000m
When you are under the power lines along the road after the cheese farm- go to your right on a 4x4 track and make a judgement on where to launch from off the steeper slope

1900m (GPS co-ords)
Normally use this launch on the far SW part of the mountain away from the power lines and easier to access. Go just past the refuge and look for the little wind streamer on the steeper gradient next to some small shrubs, park your car on the corner.
spots.going_there:
From Moutiers take the N90 road, 'Bourg saint Maurice' direction. After the tunnel go into Centron, then up to 'Montgirod' direction.
Go straight up past Montgirod on a little tar farmer road, park by the cheese farm where the tar road ends or go higher if your car can do so. It's about the same distance driving to launch as it is driving up to Forclaz(Annecy) from Doussard, meaning - roughly 15km from Centron to the launch.
spots.weather_notes:
Spring and Autumn : Hunting season, do not go to the toilet in the trees up the mountain.

Summer: Venturi in the valley.

Winter : foehn wind days-you shouldn't be out there anyway.
spots.comments:
XC :
This site starts to work early in the year as well as early in the morning. Facing SE with a very steep gradient that has little cow paddocks and forest getting that morning sun this site boasts some good thermalling opportunities. If the wind is N around to W, it is still possible to get flights in before 1pm thanks to its orientation and the micro climate of the Centon/Villette area. However when the valley system works it comes over the top joining the valley wind from Moutiers towards the high mountains from as early as 11am. BUT-It is possible to fly in the afternoon on a stable day trying to fly bubbles on the lee side especially in Autumn/Winter. 
Despite all meteo winds, every flight at about 10am, there is a light pleasant thermal breeze on launch, with a view of Tignes Grande Motte,Saint Foy,La Rosiere,les Arcs,la Plagne,Val Thorens,Meribel and Courchevel. There are various routes to take once gaining altitude with an early start to your day, some local French pilots have achieved massive distances and return triangles
If you are unlucky with the wind or arrive too late-there is a small ridge to fly from that is a good XC starting point for afternoon flying behind the Montgirod side, the launch faces W called Naves.

ACRO :
Beware : Centron houses and power lines and main road, fly acro over the trees in the left corner.
Fly with a Rogallo or Base system.
Minimum 700m in the box with bad wind, max 1000m starting at 1900m. The same distance driving to launch as driving up to Forclaz(Annecy) from Doussard, but the road is smaller, at least tar all the way up. The glide out to the 'box' can also be compared to Annecy at some (2.5 to 2.7km), this is good because most sites in the French Alps used to do 'acro ploufs' require a long glide that eats height.

spots.name: Serres Beaumont
spots.takeoff_description:
Good, early, in the morning, when the sun light the rocks which are just under the TV transmitter. 
WARNING : be very carefull before taking your decision => take off is under the north, the west and the south wind. 
WARNING : when east wind (other than brise) is facing the takeoff, it can be difficult to reach a comfortable landing. Be very carefull.
spots.going_there:
Option 1 : from MÃ©reuil, 10 minutes of car + 40 minutes by feet. 
Climb on the East side.
goto the small village called MÃ©reuil. Arriving at MÃ©reuil, continue to climb in the direction of 'La Montagne'. Just before arriving at La Montagne, leave the main road and take the forest pist named B22. If the pist is closed by the fence, you must continue by feet. 4x4 recommended. Follow B22 during 2.5km until the end of the forest pist: there is a aera where you can make a u-turn and you can park the 4x4. Then by feet climb strait in the oak/beech forest during 30 minutes. At the end of the forest, it's a little bit hard. Even if it's harder, choose the right side of the slope because on the left side, the main trail is too close from the cliff and it really dangerous, especially if you carry your aisle on your back. Continue to climb 250m until you can see the other side of the mountain (west). You are arrived.

Option 2 now forbidden by ONF (130â‚¬ fine at your own risk): from Montclus, 40 minutes of 4x4 car, 5 minutes by feet. This option is easier that the MÃ©reuil one, but the road is much longer and is now forbidden. Arriving from Serres at Monclus, take on your left and climb, climb, and climb using the forest pist which comes to the TV Transmitter. 800m before arriving to the transmitter, park the car and walk 250m on the GR94 on the opposite way of the transmitter.
spots.weather_notes: In the summer, avoid to flight after 12h00 in this area : take off can be smooth and ok while it can be very dangerous in the valley (strong brise, and too strong thermals).

spots.name: Noyers
spots.going_there: Localisation : Sur le plateau entre le déco et le chemin.
spots.comments:
Décollage:
Orientation : S
Altitude : 235m
Conditions de vol : Très bon dynamique par vent de S à SSO. Mauvais rendement par vent de SO et SE (préférer Beauvais ou St Martin). Parfois de bons thermiques permettent le départ en cross.

Dangers et difficultés : Petit site parfois très fréquenté, attention aux priorités surtout en petites conditions. En cas de « reculade » par vent fort poser le plus loin possible derrière et à droite du déco. Le rouleau y est moins méchant.

Atterrissage : Au sommet :

Dangers difficultés : Ne pas poser dans le champ et derrière les arbres (surtout à gauche). Pose facile. Accès : Du déco, descendre jusqu’à la route Noyers-Tonnerre, tourner à gauche puis à 1 km prendre à droite se garer juste après le pont.
Altitude : 170m
Remarques : Pour éviter la marche se poser dans la partie droite du pré.

spots.name: Noyers-sur-Serein (Clorges)
spots.going_there: Acces : traverser Noyers et en sortir par le NO. En sortie du village, prendre a droite puis chemin en pierre a droite (fleche parapente) pour le deco de Clorges. Pour les deux autres decos, il faut sortir de Noyers en continuant tout droit. A environ 2 km, prendre en angle un goudron qui monte legerement a une ferme (ferme de Beauvais). Le deco de Beauvais est 100m avant la ferme; celui de Clorges est accessible 200m environ apres la ferme.
spots.comments:
Orientation : SO et S 
Denivele : 70 m 
Description :  D'Ouest en Est le long de la crete :
-  deco de Clorges. 60 m. De Sud Ã  Sud-Sud/Ouest. Le deco principal. C'est 'celui du milieu', celui qui a le meilleur rendement. Il est plus simple. Pose en haut possible (niveau 2 sur l'echelle de Richter en comportant 3). Sinon pose en bas, de l'autre cote de la riviere. Pour revenir (si vous avez oublie votre pedalo), on contourne par la ferme situee a 300m sur la droite, un peu Ã  l'ouest. 
-  deco de Beauvais. 40m. SO, eventuel SO a OSO.  Ressemble a grosse pente-ecole, mais tres volable en partant du haut, meme si les rendements sont moins bons qu'a Clorges. Ligne electrique a gauche. Repose dans la pente ou pose au pied, pres de la route si besoin.  Repose en haut: niveau 1 sur l'echelle de Richter. Attention aux kekes, et aux grands arbres isoles a droite du deco. Si l'on se fait reculer il vaut mieux se decaler a droite pour aller poser derriere (moins de rouleaux)
-  deco de Venoise. Cet ancien deco oriente S/SO n'est plus pratique.
Panneaux descriptifs sur place [le gestionnaire de ce perimetre est un pilote du Club de Tonnerre AST Parapente].

spots.name: Prariond
spots.takeoff_description:
Takeoff is beside the road just before entering Prariond on the road up to La Plagne ski resort.
In effect there are 2 takeoffs separated by 100m. western one right on the corner is used by Pros in Summer (proximity to carparking)
Eastern one has a more open area without sudden dropoff.
spots.going_there:
At Aime go to Macot-la-Plagne. Then at end of village turn hard right at roundabout heading towards La Plagne. The bends are numbered starting at 21 just above Macot and reducing as you go up. After bend 10 you come out of forest into open country and parking is on right just past an approx 45 deg bend left heading to Prariond.
Pro's takeoff just behind guardrail on corner. Other one back downhill along road just past a group of trees.
spots.weather_notes: Can be turbulent in afternoon. Not often used between 1PM and 5PM
spots.comments: Weak thermal trigger areas in front of takeoff. Eastern side over Le Villard de Macot or the quarry below it. Western side over hamlets on W side of valley to W of takeoff.

spots.name: Pignu
spots.comments: Le site du Pignu est situé côté golfe de Saint Florent avec un dénivelé de 900 mètres. Le Pignu est notre site privilégié pour les baptêmes parapente et pour les vols d’initiation en soirée. Les thermiques sont généreux en journée, avec la possibilité de voir la mer des 2 côtés du Cap Corse. En soirée, le site permet un vol calme avec un panorama magnifique devant les yeux. Aucune difficulté particulière ! Interdiction de survoler les antennes (zone militaire) ! Attention le site est situé dans la TMA3 de l’aéroport de Bastia Poretta (voir carte Carte TMA3). Accès au décollage : à partir de la route qui mène aux antennes du Pignu (route à droite à 500 mètres avant le Col de Teghjime en venant de Bastia).
